brand.title: IQVIA (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — Introduction to CTFS for TechIQ

questions.question: What does CTFS stand for?
choices: Clinical Trial Financial Suite
Clinical Trial Forecasting System
Centralized Trial Finance Service
Clinical Testing Financial Solutions
questions.feedback_correct: That's right—CTFS is IQVIA's Clinical Trial Financial Suite, designed to unify financial operations across clinical trials.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The correct acronym is Clinical Trial Financial Suite. While other options sound plausible, CTFS specifically refers to IQVIA's comprehensive financial platform for trials.

questions.question: According to the course, what percentage did trial sites grow by since 2019?
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—the course notes that trial sites grew by 49% since 2019, contributing to increasing complexity in financial management.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The slide indicates that trial sites grew by 49% since 2019. You may have confused this with the 60% increase in protocol amendments.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a module or capability of the CTFS platform?
choices: Budgeting and grant management
Site and participant payments
Clinical endpoint analysis
Forecasting and reconciliation
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—clinical endpoint analysis is not part of CTFS. The platform focuses on financial functions like budgeting, payments, and reconciliation, not clinical data analysis.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Clinical endpoint analysis is not a financial function and is outside the scope of CTFS. The platform covers budgeting, contracting, payments, forecasting, and reconciliation.

questions.question: How many countries does CTFS support for participant payments?
choices: Fewer than 50
Approximately 100
More than 180
Exactly 200
questions.feedback_correct: That's correct—CTFS supports participant payments across more than 180 countries as part of its global design.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course states that CTFS extends participant payment capabilities across more than 180 countries, demonstrating its truly global scope.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of shifting from manual workflows to orchestration in CTFS?
choices: To completely eliminate human review and oversight
To focus human attention on exceptions and decisions requiring expertise rather than repetitive data handling
To speed up only the contract negotiation phase
To reduce the need for IT infrastructure
questions.feedback_correct: Excellent—orchestration aims to redirect human effort from routine tasks to high-value decisions and exception management, not to remove oversight entirely.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Orchestration is not about removing human judgment; it's about using automation to handle routine tasks so that experts can focus on issues that truly require their attention.

questions.question: According to the course, what is the estimated daily cost of delays in late-stage clinical trials?
choices: $10,000 per day
$25,000 per day
$55,000 per day
$100,000 per day
questions.feedback_correct: Right—the course cites Applied Clinical Trials data indicating that delays can cost as much as $55,000 per day in late-stage trials, underscoring the financial impact of inefficiency.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course references a specific figure from Applied Clinical Trials showing that delays in late-stage trials can cost approximately $55,000 per day.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes how CTFS uses APIs and webhooks in its architecture?
choices: They ensure CTFS never needs to integrate with external systems
They allow CTFS to connect with IQVIA capabilities, internal systems, and third-party agents to orchestrate multiple workflows
They replace the need for traditional databases
They are only used for customer reporting
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—APIs and webhooks are central to CTFS's design philosophy, enabling it to orchestrate multiple AI agents and connect with diverse systems rather than working in isolation.
questions.feedback_incorrect: APIs and webhooks in CTFS are designed to create connectivity and integration across systems, allowing the platform to orchestrate workflows with both internal and third-party capabilities.

questions.question: Based on the course content, why is it particularly important that CTFS was designed to scale modularly rather than requiring full implementation at once?
choices: Because clinical trials never use more than one module at a time
Because it allows sponsors to start with focused capabilities like site payments and expand into other workflows as needs evolve, reducing implementation complexity and risk
Because IQVIA wants to sell the modules separately at different price points
Because global regulatory requirements change so rapidly that modularity is the only viable approach
questions.feedback_correct: Excellent synthesis—modular design enables organizations to achieve immediate operational improvements with a focused pilot while building toward longer-term modernization without a disruptive big-bang implementation.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The modular approach is strategic because it allows sponsors to balance immediate operational gains with phased transformation, reducing risk and implementation burden compared to a single large-scale deployment.

questions.question: Given the course's discussion of trial complexity trends and CTFS capabilities, which scenario would present the strongest business case for implementing CTFS?
choices: A sponsor running a single-site trial in one country with stable protocols
A sponsor with multiple global sites, growing volumes of protocol amendments, fragmented financial processes causing disputes, and measurable delays in payment cycles
A sponsor that already uses spreadsheets exclusively and has no IT infrastructure
A sponsor whose primary concern is clinical data analysis rather than financial operations
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—CTFS's value is strongest when addressing multiple interrelated problems: growing complexity, fragmentation, and measurable operational impact, which aligns with the business case presented throughout the course.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course positions CTFS as most valuable when clinical trials face growing complexity, fragmented processes, and demonstrable delays—precisely the conditions that create both clinical execution risk and financial waste.
